objective: An action's declared external-effect recovery class is typed at the daemon's two-phase claim gate and honoured there: it may only narrow what the substrate would allow, ambiguity blocks the retry of every class that can land twice, and restoring local bytes never clears a pending reconciliation.
falsifiable_claim: npm run check:typed-effect-recovery pins twelve tests by exact name across two families and three source pins, proving that evaluate_claim_transition reads the canonical effect_recovery_class field, calls evaluate_claim_transition_substrate first and returns Refuse where the declared class refuses (non_retryable at all, compensatable before its compensation, any ambiguity-blocked class) while never turning a substrate Refuse into a Grant; that RecoveryClass::parse is closed over exactly the ontology action contract's frozen member set and refuses an undeclared class rather than defaulting; and that effect_is_reconciled requires an external_system_readback source with a landed/did-not-land outcome, so a restore leaves the ambiguity standing. npm run mutate:typed-effect-recovery plants six defects and requires each to go red. The check is CI-BOUND: ci.yml runs it in build_and_test immediately after the daemon's whole suite, so deleting or renaming any of the twelve tests is red rather than quiet.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Six planted defects, each required to turn the check red and each restored byte-for-byte: the class defaults to replayable instead of refusing an undeclared effect; the ambiguity block is disabled for reconciliation_required; any reconciliation source counts, so a restore clears an ambiguity; RESTART, where an orphaned claim from a dead incarnation is re-granted instead of reconciled; the frozen canonical member set is widened on one side only; and the declared class stops narrowing the claim so the module becomes uncalled.
remaining_nonclaims: The class is honoured where an action DECLARES it. An admission carrying no effect_recovery_class keeps the two-phase substrate's own decision; this unit does not retroactively assign a class to effects that never declared one, so 'every action declares its recovery class' is not yet true of every producer.
The proof is at the claim gate and is pure: no live external system, no provider, no clock. Provider-side recovery, the reconciliation planner and the receipt contracts named in canon remain planned.

The work lifecycle log's cancellation planner (M04.6) matches the same effect_recovery_class field against a DIFFERENT vocabulary (none, reversible, compensatable, irreversible, ambiguous). That divergence is recorded, not resolved here: it belongs to M04.6's owner.
backup/restore remains its own check (check:backup-restore); this unit proves only that a restore does not satisfy reconciliation, which is the claim canon makes about it.
